output.reason: Several weeks of intermittent post-fatty-meal right upper quadrant pain without reported fever or jaundice suggests possible gallstone disease needing a clinician to arrange ultrasound and follow-up, but nothing reported requires emergency or same-day hands-on care.
output.patientMessage: Ask a Counsel clinician in this thread to review your symptoms and arrange a gallbladder ultrasound in the coming days; pain that repeatedly follows fatty meals often comes from gallstones, which needs imaging rather than messaging alone. Meanwhile, eating lower-fat meals may reduce attacks. Go to an emergency department if pain lasts more than a few hours, becomes severe or constant, or you develop fever, vomiting, or yellowing of your skin or eyes.
differential: Peptic ulcer disease or other upper GI cause
